ts plot¶

plot draws the two plots that guide time-series modelling: the autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions with their white-noise confidence band, and the residuals against time. Each has two forms: a *_payload function returning the plotted numbers (for your own tables or plotting), and a drawing function that adds the picture to a pluss::pl::Studio figure, which can be saved as SVG, PDF or PNG (save_svg(path), save_pdf(path), save_png(path, dpi)).

The Surface¶

Entity

What it gives you

CorrPlotOptions

Options of the autocorrelation plots and payloads

CorrPlotPayload

The numbers behind an autocorrelation plot

plot_acf

Draws the autocorrelation plot of a series into a pluss::pl::Studio figure

plot_acf_payload

The numbers behind the autocorrelation plot: lags, values and the white-noise band

plot_pacf

Draws the partial autocorrelation plot of a series into a pluss::pl::Studio figure

plot_pacf_payload

The numbers behind the partial autocorrelation plot: lags, values and the white-noise band

plot_residuals

Draws the residuals of a model against time into a pluss::pl::Studio figure

plot_residuals_payload

The numbers behind a residual plot: the time index and the residuals

ResidualPlotOptions

The numbers behind a residual plot

How To Call It¶

Compute the numbers behind the autocorrelation plot of an autoregressive series.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = ar1(300, 0.7);
  ts::plot::CorrPlotOptions options;
  options.max_lag = 4;
  const auto payload = ts::plot::acf_payload(y, options);
  const auto lags = payload.lags.host<std::int64_t>();
  const auto values = payload.values.host<double>();
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lags.size(); ++i) std::cout << "lag " << lags[i] << "  " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(3) << values[i] << "\n";
  std::cout << "95% band: +/- " << payload.conf_high << "\n";
}

Output

lag 1  0.700
lag 2  0.486
lag 3  0.414
lag 4  0.357
95% band: +/- 0.113
